title: From average speed to instant speed
objectives: Shrink a secant into a tangent to find an instantaneous rate of change.
Compute an average rate of change as the slope of a secant.

screens.title: From average speed to instant speed
screens.prose: A speedometer shows one number at one instant. But speed is distance over time, and an instant has no time in it. We will settle that puzzle by shrinking a window.
A stone is dropped from a cliff. After $t$ seconds it has fallen $s = 5t^2$ metres. P and Q are two moments on the curve; drag them along it.

derive.caption: From P to Q the stone falls {{round(Q.y - P.y, 2)}} m in {{round(Q.x - P.x, 2)}} s

screens.question: Drag P to $t = 1$ and Q to $t = 3$. What is the stone's average speed between them?

widget.label: Average speed from t = 1 to t = 3
widget.accept: 20 m/s: a fall of 40 m in 2 s.

hints.text: Average speed is the distance covered divided by the time taken.
Read the caption: how far does the stone fall between P and Q, and in how long?
At $t = 1$ it has fallen 5 m and at $t = 3$ it has fallen 45 m. That is 40 m in 2 s.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the distance fallen between P and Q by the time between them.

byKey.height-over-time: You divided 45 m by 3 s. That is the average since the drop, not between P and Q.
byKey.half-run: You divided 45 m by 2 s. Subtract the 5 m already fallen at P first.
byKey.no-divide: 40 m is how far the stone fell. Divide by the 2 s it took.

explain.text: The stone fell $45 - 5 = 40$ m in $3 - 1 = 2$ s, so it averaged 20 m/s. That is the slope of the line PQ: rise over run. A steeper line means a faster average.

canvas.caption: From P to Q the stone falls 40 m in 2 s

screens.prose: Now fix P at $t = 2$ and put Q a gap of $h$ seconds later. The dashed line runs through P and Q. Slide $h$ down towards 0 and watch the caption.

derive.caption: Gap $h$ = {{fixed(h, 2)}} s. Average speed from P to Q: {{fixed((5 * pow(2 + h, 2) - 20) / h, 2)}} m/s

screens.question: As $h$ shrinks, what does the average speed settle towards?

options.text: 0 m/s, because the gap shrinks to nothing
options.why: You watched the fall from P to Q shrink to nothing. The time shrinks too, and their ratio stays near 20.

options.text: 20 m/s

options.why: That is the average for the widest gap, $h = 1.5$. Keep sliding towards 0.

options.text: Nothing: at $h = 0$ the fraction is $0/0$
options.why: True at $h = 0$ itself, but we never go there. Every small $h$ gives a value, and those values crowd round 20.

hints.text: Slide $h$ to 1, then 0.5, then 0.1, and read the speed each time.
Watch the digits after the decimal point as $h$ gets small.
At $h = 0.1$ the caption reads 20.50; at $h = 0.01$ it reads 20.05.

feedback.correct: The averages close in on 20 m/s.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read the caption for several small values of $h$.

byKey.zero: You let the distance shrink but not the time. Both shrink, and their ratio stays near 20.
byKey.undefined: You put $h = 0$ in directly. We only ask what the averages approach as $h$ gets small.

explain.text: At $h = 0.01$ the average is 20.05 m/s, and smaller gaps get closer still to 20. The dashed line has swung onto the line that just touches the curve at P. Its slope, 20, is the stone's speed at the instant $t = 2$.

canvas.caption: Gap $h$ = 0.01 s. Average speed from P to Q: 20.05 m/s

screens.prose: A line through two points of a curve is a **secant**. As $h$ shrinks, the secant swings onto the **tangent**, the line that just touches the curve at P. At $t = 2$ the stone has fallen $s(2) = 20$ m.

state.caption: Secant for $h = 1$ (dashed) and the tangent at P

screens.question: Fill in the average speed $\dfrac{s(2+h) - s(2)}{h}$ for each gap.

hints.text: For $h = 1$: the stone falls $45 - 20 = 25$ m in 1 s, so 25 m/s. Do the same for each row.
Subtract 20 m from each $s(2+h)$ before you divide.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. For each row, subtract 20 from $s(2+h)$, then divide by $h$.

byKey.r1c2: For $h = 0.1$: subtract 20 from 22.05 to get 2.05 m, then divide by 0.1 s.
byKey.r2c2: For $h = 0.01$: subtract 20 from 20.2005 to get 0.2005 m, then divide by 0.01 s.
byKey.r3c2: For $h = 0.001$: subtract 20 from 20.020005 to get 0.020005 m, then divide by 0.001 s.

explain.text: Each average is $20 + 5h$: 20.5, 20.05, 20.005. The extra $5h$ dies away, so the averages close in on 20 m/s. That limit is the **instantaneous speed**: the slope of the tangent at P.

screens.prose: Q can sit before P too. Take $h = -0.1$, so Q is at $t = 1.9$, where the stone has fallen $s(1.9) = 18.05$ m.
screens.question: What is $\dfrac{s(2+h) - s(2)}{h}$ for $h = -0.1$?

widget.label: Average speed from t = 1.9 to t = 2

hints.text: Put $s(1.9) = 18.05$ and $s(2) = 20$ into the fraction.
The top is $18.05 - 20$, and the bottom is $-0.1$.
$\dfrac{-1.95}{-0.1}$: two negatives give a positive.

feedback.correct: The stone fell 1.95 m in the 0.1 s before P: 19.5 m/s.

byKey.sign: You kept one minus sign. The top and the bottom are both negative, so the result is positive.
byKey.other-side: That is the gap after P, from the last screen. Here Q comes before P.
byKey.no-divide: 1.95 m is the fall. Divide it by the 0.1 s it took.

explain.text: From the left the averages sit just under 20: 19.5 at $h = -0.1$. From the right they sit just over: 20.5 at $h = 0.1$. Both sides squeeze the same number, so the instantaneous speed is 20 m/s.

screens.prose: Move to a new instant, $t = 3$, where the stone has fallen 45 m. Shrink the gap $h$ again.

derive.caption: Gap $h$ = {{fixed(h, 2)}} s. Average speed: {{fixed((5 * pow(3 + h, 2) - 45) / h, 2)}} m/s

screens.question: How fast is the stone falling at the instant $t = 3$?

hints.text: Slide $h$ close to 0 and read the average speed.
At $h = 0.01$ the caption reads 30.05.
The averages are $30 + 5h$, so they close in on 30.

feedback.correct: The averages close in on 30 m/s.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Shrink $h$ and see where the average speed heads.

byKey.height: 45 m is how far the stone has fallen, the height of P. Speed is the slope there.
byKey.from-start: You divided 45 m by 3 s. That is the average since the drop; the stone is faster now.
byKey.wide: 35 m/s is the average over a whole second after P. Shrink the gap.

explain.text: The averages are $30 + 5h$, so they close in on 30 m/s. At $t = 2$ the speed was 20 m/s, so the stone gains 10 m/s every second. That is gravity at work.

screens.prose: Sam says: at $t = 2$ the stone has fallen 20 m in 2 s. So its speed at that instant is $20 \div 2 = 10$ m/s.
screens.question: What is the stone's speed at $t = 2$, and what went wrong for Sam?

options.text: 10 m/s: Sam is right, speed is distance over time
options.why: You divided all the distance by all the time. That is the slope of the dashed line from the start, not the tangent at P.

options.text: 20 m/s: Sam found the average since the drop, but the stone has sped up
0 m/s: at an instant no time passes, so nothing moves
options.why: You set the gap to zero. We never do; we watch the averages as the gap shrinks, and they head to 20.

options.text: 15 m/s: use the last second, from $t = 1$ to $t = 2$
options.why: That is closer, but still an average over a whole second. Shrinking the window pushes it up to 20.

hints.text: Is the stone moving at a steady speed, or speeding up?
Compare the dashed line with the line that touches the curve at P.
Sam's 10 m/s is the slope from the start to P. On the earlier screens the averages near $t = 2$ closed in on 20.

feedback.correct: Correct. 10 m/s is an average over the whole fall.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which speed did the shrinking windows give at $t = 2$?

byKey.sam: You divided total distance by total time, as Sam did. That averages over the slow start; the speed at $t = 2$ is 20 m/s.

explain.text: Sam's 10 m/s is the slope of the dashed line from the start: an average over the whole fall. The stone began at rest and sped up, so it is going faster than its average. The tangent at P has slope 20.

screens.prose: For any function $f$, the average rate of change from $a$ to $a + h$ is the slope of the secant. Shrinking $h$ gives the **instantaneous rate of change** at $a$: $$\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}$$ It is the slope of the tangent at $a$.
screens.question: What does $h \to 0$ ask us to do?

options.text: Find the value the fraction approaches as $h$ gets small, without setting $h = 0$
Put $h = 0$ into the fraction
options.why: You put $h = 0$ in directly, which gives $0/0$. On the table you never did that: you watched 20.5, 20.05, 20.005.

options.text: Use the smallest $h$ a calculator allows and stop there
options.why: Any fixed $h$ still gives an average, such as 20.005. The limit is the number the averages approach: exactly 20.

hints.text: On the table, did you ever use $h = 0$?
You used $h$ = 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001, and watched the averages approach 20.

feedback.correct: The limit is where the averages are heading.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about what you did with the table of gaps.

explain.text: You never set $h = 0$: the fraction would be $0/0$. You watched 20.5, 20.05, 20.005 and named the number they approach. That number is the limit.

screens.prose: The table suggested the average over a gap $h$ is $20 + 5h$. Now prove it with algebra, then let $h \to 0$.
screens.question: Put the lines of the derivation in order.

hints.text: Start by putting the formula for $s$ into the fraction.
Expand the bracket before anything cancels.
Put in $s$, expand, cancel the 20s, divide by $h$, then let $h$ shrink.

feedback.correct: Each line follows from the one above.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. You cannot cancel or divide until the bracket is expanded.

byKey.divide: Dividing by $h$ needs every term on top to carry an $h$. That happens only after the 20s cancel.
byKey.limit: The limit comes last. Before dividing by $h$, setting $h = 0$ gives $0/0$.

explain.text: Expanding and cancelling left $20h + 5h^2$, where every term has a factor $h$. Dividing by $h$ gave $20 + 5h$, exactly the pattern in your table. Only then is $h \to 0$ safe, and it gives 20.

screens.prose: A share's price during a morning follows roughly $P(t) = 100 + 5t - t^2$ pounds, $t$ hours after the open. At $t = 2$ it is £106.00. The table gives the change per hour over windows that shrink towards $t = 2$.
screens.question: What is the price's instantaneous rate of change at $t = 2$, in pounds per hour?

widget.label: Rate of change at t = 2, pounds per hour

hints.text: Which number are the windows closing in on?
From the right the rates rise: 0.00, 0.50, 0.90. From the left the rate is 1.10.
The rates are $1 - h$ for a window of length $h$. As $h \to 0$ they approach 1.

feedback.correct: The window rates squeeze £1.00 per hour from both sides.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the number the change per hour approaches as the window shrinks.

byKey.level: £106.00 is the price itself, the height of the curve. The rate is how fast it is moving.
byKey.widest: £0.00 is the rate over the whole hour, when the price went up and came back. Shrink the window.
byKey.last-right: £0.90 is still an average over 6 minutes. The left window gives £1.10, so the limit sits between.
byKey.last-left: £1.10 is still an average over 6 minutes. The right window gives £0.90, so the limit sits between.

explain.text: The rates over windows after $t = 2$ climb 0.00, 0.50, 0.90, and the window before gives 1.10. Each is $1 - h$, so they close in on £1.00 per hour. A desk would call that the price's instantaneous drift at 2 hours.

ideas: An average rate of change is the slope of a secant: the change in output over the change in input.
Shrinking the gap $h$ swings the secant onto the tangent. The averages close in on one number from both sides.
That number is the instantaneous rate of change at $a$: the slope of the tangent there.

formula.name: Instantaneous rate of change
formula.note: Never put $h = 0$ in directly: it gives $0/0$. Simplify first, then let $h$ shrink.

summary.trap: Total distance over total time is the average since the start, not the speed now. Shrink a window around the instant itself.

quiz.prose: A stone falls $s = 5t^2$ metres in $t$ seconds.
quiz.question: What is its average speed from $t = 1$ to $t = 2$?

widget.label: Average speed
widget.accept: 15 m/s: a fall of 15 m in 1 s.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract the distances at the two times, then divide by the time between.

byKey.from-start: You divided 20 m by 2 s, the average since the drop. Start the window at $t = 1$.
byKey.height: 20 m is how far it has fallen by $t = 2$. Subtract the 5 m fallen by $t = 1$.

explain.text: At $t = 1$ the stone has fallen 5 m and at $t = 2$ it has fallen 20 m. That is 15 m in 1 s, an average of 15 m/s.

quiz.prose: For $f(x) = x^2$, the secant slope from $x = 3$ to $x = 3 + h$ simplifies to $6 + h$.
quiz.question: What is the slope of the tangent at $x = 3$?

options.why: You found $f(3)$, the height of the curve. The slope is what $6 + h$ approaches.
You put $h = 1$, which is one secant. Let $h$ shrink towards 0.

options.text: No value: $h = 0$ gives $0/0$
options.why: The simplified form $6 + h$ has no fraction left. As $h \to 0$ it approaches 6.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Let $h$ shrink in $6 + h$.

explain.text: The secant slope $6 + h$ approaches 6 as $h$ shrinks. So the tangent at $x = 3$ has slope 6, while the curve's height there is 9.

quiz.prose: A share trades at £84.00 at 11:00. Its change per hour over windows starting then is £2.30 over 1 hour and £2.03 over 6 minutes. Over 36 seconds it is £2.003.
quiz.question: What is the price's instantaneous rate of change at 11:00?

options.text: £2.00 per hour
£2.003 per hour
options.why: You took the shortest window. It is still an average; the rates are heading to 2.00.

options.text: £2.30 per hour
options.why: You took the widest window, the roughest average. Shrink it.

options.text: £84.00 per hour
options.why: £84.00 is the price itself, not how fast it is changing.

feedback.correct: 2.30, 2.03, 2.003: the extra part shrinks tenfold each time.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the number the rates approach.

explain.text: Each tenfold shrink of the window cuts the extra above £2.00 tenfold: 0.30, 0.03, 0.003. The rates approach £2.00 per hour, the instantaneous rate.

quiz.prose: Take a fixed $h = 0.5$ in the fraction $\dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}$.
quiz.question: What does the fraction measure?

options.text: The slope of the secant from $a$ to $a + 0.5$
The slope of the tangent at $a$
options.why: Only the limit as $h \to 0$ gives the tangent. With $h = 0.5$ it is still an average.

options.text: The height of the curve at $a$
options.why: The height is $f(a)$ alone. The fraction divides a change in height by a change in $x$.

options.text: The change in $f$ from $a$ to $a + 0.5$
options.why: That is only the top of the fraction. Dividing by $h$ turns it into a rate.

feedback.correct: A fixed $h$ gives an average rate: a secant slope.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. With $h$ fixed, the fraction is rise over run between two points.

explain.text: With $h$ fixed at 0.5, the fraction is the rise from $a$ to $a + 0.5$ over the run 0.5. That is the secant's slope, the average rate of change. The tangent comes only in the limit.
